jobs.title: Associate Consultant, Private Equity, Strategic Transformation
jobs.description:
ASSOCIATE CONSULTANT, PRIVATE EQUITY, STRATEGIC TRANSFORMATION



About Chartis

The challenges facing US healthcare are longstanding and all too familiar. We are Chartis, and we believe in better. We work with more than 1,900 organizations annually to develop and activate transformative strategies, operating models, and organizational enterprises that make US healthcare more affordable, accessible, safe, and human. With more than 1,450 professionals, we help providers, payers, technology innovators, retail companies, and investors create and embrace solutions that tangibly and materially reshape healthcare for the better. Our family of brands—Chartis, Jarrard, Greeley, and HealthScape Advisors—is 100% focused on healthcare and each has a longstanding commitment to helping transform healthcare in big and small ways. Believe in better.

 

Chartis has offices in Boston, Chicago, New York, Washington D.C., and Nashville.

For this role, we are currently targeting candidates in Chicago, Boston, and the greater New York area, including New York City and nearby markets such as Philadelphia.

Remote work is allowed.

 

Minimal travel is expected.



Role Overview

We are actively seeking an experienced Associate Consultant to join Chartis in the Private Equity Advisory Practice. Associate Consultants are integral members of our consulting teams, generally working on a single engagement to meet client needs while under the direction of and collaborating closely with Engagement Managers and Consultants. Associate Consultants are responsible for effectively planning and managing distinct segments of work, while acting as a valued contributor to the team. Chartis’ PE Advisory Practice works with healthcare institutional investors and their portfolio companies to help them uncover and realize unique value across the full lifecycle of their investments. Our offerings in this space encompass transaction diligence, platform integration and optimization services, and growth and exit strategy development.



Responsibilities

 - Define analytic approaches, integrating multiple analyses, and develop analytic understanding of client problems to identify issues and opportunities to motivate client action 

 - Gather and refine complex data sets and data sources to enable accurate and robust quantitative analyses 

 - Provide insight into hypotheses under consideration and contribute to team's understanding of client's overall problem and potential solutions 

 - Support consulting team by delivering against commitments on time 

 - Create elegant, multi-issue client communications, present analytic findings and recommendations, and field client questions with minimal support 

 - Contribute to firm’s knowledge development by capturing client engagement approaches and insights.
   
   

Qualifications and Desired Skills

 - 2+ years with a strategy consulting, strategic planning/corporate strategy group, or private equity/venture capital firm

 - Advanced degree preferred (e.g. MHA, MPH) 

 - Strong project management skills with experience working on multiple work streams

 - Demonstrated collaboration, project management, problem-solving, quantitative and qualitative analysis skills

 - Strong critical thinking skills; ability to develop solutions that address client needs

 - Succinct communicator who thinks well on feet and tailors communication to audience

 - Comfortable manipulating and synthesizing data

 - Experience working and leading in a team environment

 - Highly knowledgeable about healthcare landscape and current trends in healthcare

 - Genuine passion for and commitment to the transformation of healthcare delivery

 - Responds well to and enjoys change; works well under pressure

 - Flexibility to travel as required, remote work is allowed



Salary range: $121,500-$143,000, plus may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus. The salary range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills, experience, training, licensure and certifications, practice area, and other business and organizational needs. In addition, Chartis offers several benefits including medical, dental, vision, HSA, FSA, disability insurance, life insurance, 401(k) match, paid time off, wellness stipend, and additional voluntary benefits.

At Chartis, we pride ourselves on having a diverse workforce. We value and celebrate the uniqueness of individuals and the different perspectives they provide. We offer equal opportunity employment regardless of race, color, religion, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability status, age, marital status, or protected veteran status

jobs.title: Engagement Manager, Financial Performance Improvement
jobs.description:
ENGAGEMENT MANAGER, FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENT



About Chartis

Chartis comprises 1,000 professionals who value working for a purpose-driven organization, people who have committed their careers to helping providers, payers, technology innovators, retail companies, and investors create and embrace solutions that reshape healthcare for the better. We work with over 900 clients annually to help make US healthcare more affordable, accessible, safe, and human. 



Through our family of brands—Chartis, Jarrard, Greeley, and HealthScape Advisors—we have created a culture that prioritizes respect for our clients, commitment to each other, and unwavering integrity. From physicians, nurses, healthcare executives, and community health leaders to strategists, digital advisors, transactions experts, and healthcare futurists, we bring a diverse set of perspectives to assess healthcare challenges from every angle. 



Believing in what we do helps us attract and retain the best and brightest because the work we do every day makes a meaningful impact. This theme of believing in a better way forward is woven into our brand, Believe in better. 



Chartis has offices in Boston, Chicago, New York, Washington D.C., and Nashville. 

Remote work is allowed. On average, 25%-50% client travel is required.  #LI-Remote



Role Overview

We are actively seeking experienced healthcare management consultants to join Chartis as Engagement Managers within our Financial Performance Improvement Practice within our Financial Transformation line of business. Engagement Managers are integral members of our consulting teams, leading Analysts, Associate Consultants and Consultants on projects with healthcare provider clients typically spanning 6-9 months in duration.



Our typical Financial Performance Improvement engagements bring together colleagues from across the firm (e.g., Clinical, Digital & Technology, and Strategic Transformation Lines of Business) to deliver comprehensive and sustainable enterprise transformation services to help our clients meet their clinical, financial, and operational goals. 



Responsibilities

 - Leading the problem-solving process and day-to-day management of the project team, including overseeing the team’s analyses and deliverables

 - Managing the overall project, balancing work effort and input from clients and colleagues across different levels and lines of business to achieve goals

 - Acting as a trusted advisor to clients, drawing upon healthcare knowledge, experience and insights

 - Creating sophisticated, compelling deliverables that motivate clients to action

 - Coaching and mentoring junior staff, rapidly developing their skills and knowledge through an apprenticeship-based development model

 - Supporting the firm’s growth through contributions to talent initiatives, solution development, thought leadership, and other areas



Qualifications and Desired Skills

 - At least 6 years of experience working with healthcare providers on financial and operational performance improvement and/or post-merger integration operational initiatives, including 3+ years managing others

 - Experience in leading comprehensive financial and operational improvement engagements or leading work teams within the overall engagement (e.g., workforce, supply chain, provider enterprise, procedural, throughput and patient flow, etc.)

 - Advanced degree preferred (e.g., MBA, MHA, MPH)

 - Excellent critical thinking and analytical skills

 - Outstanding verbal and written communication skills, able to share insights in a way that motivates clients to action

 - Strong people leader, adept at managing team’s work while developing colleagues’ capabilities

 - Advanced skills in Excel, Tableau, and PowerPoint

 - Strong entrepreneurial drive with desire to challenge the status quo, develop new solutions, and support methodology advancement

 - Passion for improving the delivery of healthcare



Salary range: $192,000-$248,000, plus may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus. The salary range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including, but not limited to, skills, experience, training, licensure and certifications, practice area, and other business and organizational needs. In addition, Chartis offers several benefits including medical, dental, vision, HSA, FSA, disability insurance, life insurance, 401(k) match, paid time off, wellness stipend, and additional voluntary benefits.



At Chartis, we pride ourselves on having a diverse workforce. We value and celebrate the uniqueness of individuals and the different perspectives the provide. ROLE OVERVIEW

As Director of Talent Development, you will lead strategic talent development initiatives and serve as a key partner to our Professional Services Team (PST). Reporting to the AVP of Talent Development, you will play a pivotal role in designing and executing talent development programs that support career growth, organizational effectiveness, and business alignment. You will work closely with the Enterprise Architecture team to ensure that our talent development data is accurate, actionable and aligned with the business needs. This role is ideal for a strategic leader with a passion for people development and experience in people analytics.

● Lead the design and delivery of high-impact talent development initiatives - such as onboarding, colleague engagement, leadership development, and coaching and mentoring programs - that support colleague career progression and foster long term colleague engagement

● Develop relationships with Professional Services Team (PST) leadership and colleagues to understand development needs, career aspirations, and emerging talent challenges, while coaching managers on performance and team dynamics to strengthen leadership capability and consistency across the firm

● Lead the firm's performance management processes for PST (e.g., 90-day feedback, annual reviews, upward feedback) in collaboration with calibration committees and ensure alignment with talent development strategy

● Partner with the Enterprise Architecture team to design, implement, and continuously improve the integrated systems and tools that support talent processes, enhance data quality, and enable data-driven decision-making

● Analyze talent development trends, forecasts, and capability gaps; provide recommendations to leadership on investments, program design, and organizational development priorities

● Serve as a strategic partner to recruiting, learning, finance, and talent operations teams to ensure talent development initiatives are integrated with broader people strategy

● Develop and mentor the talent development team, fostering a culture of continuous improvement, data literacy, and strategic thinking

● Demonstrate an understanding of our DEIB tenets and a commitment to our firm's core values in daily interactions




QUALIFICATIONS AND DESIRED SKILLS

● Bachelor’s degree in business or related field required; Master’s degree preferred

● 8+ years of progressive experience in talent development, people operations, or human resources

● Demonstrated experience with people analytics, data-driven decision-making, and translating data into actionable insights

● Experience in professional services, management consulting, or similar knowledge-intensive environments

● Proven expertise in designing and implementing talent development programs, including leadership development, coaching, and performance management

● Strong strategic thinker with the ability to see connections between talent development, business strategy, and organizational performance

● Proven ability to navigate ambiguity and bring structure to new or evolving areas, with a focus on process improvement

● Excellent project management and systems thinking skills; ability to manage complexity while maintaining clarity

● Strong leadership presence and credibility; demonstrated ability to lead teams and drive organizational change and influence senior leaders to achieve buy-in

● Technologically savvy with experience implementing and optimizing HR systems and tools; comfort with data analytics tools and platforms

● High level of emotional intelligence; demonstrated ability to build trust, show empathy, coach effectively, and develop others

● Outstanding judgment, maturity, and integrity in handling confidential and sensitive information

jobs.description:
About Chartis

The challenges facing US healthcare are longstanding and all too familiar. We are Chartis, and we believe in better. We work with more than 1,900 organizations annually to develop and activate transformative strategies, operating models, and organizational enterprises that make US healthcare more affordable, accessible, safe, and human. Believe in better.



Chartis has offices in Boston, Chicago, New York, Washington D.C., and Nashville.



Role Overview

Chartis is seeking a Director of Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) to join our Finance team. This role will partner closely with senior leaders across the business to connect strategy, operations, and financial performance. The Director will help shape business plans, lead forecasting and performance analysis, and provide insights that support growth, profitability, and sound decision-making.

This is an opportunity for a finance leader who enjoys working across functions, building trusted relationships, and turning complex data into clear business direction. The ideal candidate brings strong analytical and financial planning capabilities, sound judgment, and the ability to influence leaders in a dynamic, growth-oriented environment.



Responsibilities

 - Serve as a trusted finance partner to business and functional leaders, building a strong understanding of strategy, growth priorities, operating drivers, and financial performance

 - Translate business priorities into financial targets, operating plans, and measurable outcomes

 - Provide insights and recommendations related to growth, profitability, workforce planning, investments, and other key business decisions

 - Support strategic and operational discussions with a balanced perspective on performance, talent, and long-term business goals

 - Develop clear financial narratives that help leaders understand results, risks, opportunities, and required actions

 - Lead financial planning and forecasting for supported areas, including revenue, profitability, headcount, and other key operating drivers

 - Partner with leaders to develop annual budgets and longer-term financial plans aligned with strategic priorities

 - Challenge assumptions thoughtfully and ensure plans reflect both opportunities and execution risks

 - Establish and monitor KPIs that connect commercial activity, delivery performance, workforce capacity, and financial outcomes

 - Partner with leadership on initiatives to improve pricing, project economics, resource deployment, and overall profitability

 - Help build a scalable finance business-partnering model as the organization continues to grow

 - Partner across Finance, Accounting, Talent, Operations, and other functions to improve data quality, reporting, and decision-making

 - Develop tools, frameworks, and performance metrics that support consistency while allowing for different business needs

ROLE OVERVIEW

As Chartis accelerates its evolution into a more tech and AI-forward enterprise, this role sits within the Strategic Intelligence & Technology (SIT) organization—built to enable internal and external transformation through modern technology, data, and analytics capabilities that advance healthcare AI and digital transformation and deliver new insights to our clients.

Specifically, this role sits within SIT’s Analytics & Insights team, helping shape and deliver increasingly sophisticated analytic deliverables and insights to our clients while also contributing to reusable analytics assets that can be deployed and tailored to specific client use cases.

This specific role will be focused on supporting our Revenue Cycle Transformation practice. This role bridges consulting teams, business stakeholders, and technical resources by acquiring, preparing, and analyzing client data, delivering exploratory insights, upskilling our consulting teams in advanced analytical practice, and supporting the design of scalable solutions in partnership with solutions leads and engineering. This role is a foundational member of the analytics delivery team, combining hands-on SQL and business intelligence (BI) skills with business consulting acumen to ensure data-driven insights are rapidly available to projects, and we advance as a practice in bringing best-in-class insights to the market for our clients.




RESPONSIBILITIES

Client Data Acquisition & Preparation

 - Partner with client teams to extract and acquire structured data based on our inventory of SQL code, along with non-SQL based data needs in the future.

 - Support extract, transfer, load (ETL) process with a high-touch customer service model to acquire and transmit data

 - Write basic SQL scripts for data extraction and mapping.

 - Perform first-level cleaning and QA (deduplication, schema alignment, missing values).

 - Manage data from SFTP through to analytics deployment in internal analytics platform (Echo).

Exploratory Analysis & Insights

 - Conduct exploratory/first-pass analysis to uncover trends and issues.

 - Deliver stop-gap dashboards or ad-hoc reports in Power BI/Tableau to support project needs.

 - Prepare first-pass deliverables for consulting teams on analytics findings.

Solution Support & Enablement

 - Collaborate with Domain Data Engineers to codify business rules into advanced SQL extraction and data build tools (DBT) and with BI Engineers to create impactful data visualization and storytelling.

 - Support Solutions Leads in designing analytic solutions that align with client process improvement goals.

 - Coach consulting and client teams on BI tool functionality and analytic interpretation.

 - Provide feedback on data quality and business logic for continuous improvement.




QUALIFICATIONS AND DESIRED SKILLS

 - 5-8 years of relevant analytics experience, with a minimum of 2 years in a professional related healthcare field is required.

 - Working knowledge of Epic Clarity database; Clarity/Cogito certification (or equivalent) is required.

 - Bachelor’s Degree in a quantitative or technology-related field of study (e.g., Business, Mathematics, Economics, Statistics, Analytics, or Informatics).

 - Previous experience executing analytics with programming languages (e.g., SQL, Python, R, Spark, PySpark, Scala) with deployment via notebook tools (e.g., Jupyter, Zeppelin)

 - Proficiency in SQL for querying, data extraction, and basic transformations.

 - Familiarity with BI tools (Power BI, Tableau). Exposure to Snowflake or other cloud-based data platforms preferred.

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, applying quantitative techniques to identify trends, diagnose issues, and developing evidence-based recommendations.

 - Skilled collaborator who partners effectively with client teams to frame data challenges, co-develop solutions, and substantiate recommendations with data-driven insights.

 - Proven ability to independently manage workstreams or projects, demonstrating initiative, accountability, and exceptional attention to detail.

We are lucky to have extraordinarily talented people working in our firm – all brought together around our unifying mission, a shared dedication to our core values, and the emphasis we place on creating an environment that enriches the experiences of our clients, our colleagues and our communities. In this way, we find that we are remarkably aligned with our clients. And that has made for achieving some truly great things.

ROLE OVERVIEW

Engagement Managers are the day-to-day leaders of HealthScape’s payer transformation engagements. They combine healthcare payer expertise, structured problem solving, and disciplined project leadership to help clients navigate strategic and operational challenges. Engagement Managers direct analysis, translate findings into actionable recommendations, manage client relationships, and develop consulting teams across a variety of payer-focused engagements.

 - Develop business cases, operating model recommendations, transformation roadmaps, governance structures, and implementation plans that account for organizational capabilities and execution constraints.

 - Support proposals, client development, thought leadership, knowledge sharing, and the evolution of HealthScape’s payer transformation offerings.




QUALIFICATIONS AND DESIRED SKILLS

 - 6+ years of healthcare consulting experience; experience serving health plans or other payer organizations strongly preferred.

 - Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred.

 - Understanding of health plan business models, payer economics, and strategic and operational challenges across the healthcare ecosystem.

 - Demonstrated experience leading consulting workstreams or engagements, managing teams, and delivering high-quality client outcomes.
